data.text: The VR tour's design was framed by objectives such as capturing heritage and minimizing cybersickness, while accounting for the risk of cybersickness in large geographic areas. An iterative design-prototype-evaluate cycle was used to refine the design based on visitor behaviors and feedback. This process informed choices about locations, user groups, and navigation, eventually leading to features like a minimap and notification system.
points: The VR tour's design was framed by objectives like capturing heritage and minimizing cybersickness.
A large geographic spread can lead to cybersickness because exploration requires time.
An iterative design-prototype-evaluate cycle was used to refine ideas based on user feedback.
Visitor behaviors and preferences informed decisions on locations, user groups, and navigation.
Feedback led to the inclusion of elements like a minimap, a notification system, and user controls.

data.text: Identifying users is the first stage of user experience design so that the experience can be designed accordingly. The virtual tour's content and features were tailored to the preferences of three distinct user categories identified through contextual inquiry. By covering all 24 identified information points, the tour comprehensively captures the tangible and intangible heritage of the island.
points: Identifying users is the first stage of user experience design.
Content and features are tailored to the preferences of specific user categories identified through contextual inquiry.
Information points are identified through user interaction, field trips, and feedback.
The virtual tour covers 24 specific information points.
The tour covers all 24 points to capture the island's tangible and intangible heritage.

data.text: The virtual tour starts with an immersive curved screen that shows an introductory video and a system tutorial. A 360-degree boat ride video then simulates the experience of being transported from the mainland to the island. Finally, users select a group category, such as pilgrims, students, or tourists, before the tour begins.
points: An immersive curved screen shows an introductory video and a system tutorial.
A 360-degree boat ride video simulates being transported from the mainland to the island.
Users select a group category before the tour starts.

data.text: Preprocessing images and videos involved using high-resolution content and removing unwanted elements. These media were edited for uniform illumination to prevent the user from feeling that something is odd. Ambient sounds were also added based on the location to create an authentic ambience.
points: Preprocessing images and videos involved using high-resolution content and removing unwanted elements.
Images and videos were edited for uniform illumination to prevent the user from feeling that something is odd.
Ambient sounds were added based on the location to create an authentic ambience.

data.text: The virtual tablet interface acts as the main interface for navigation tools, a video player, and information content. It includes navigation tools like a left-side island map and a video player with various controls. Information content is accessed through info elements, and the design is inspired by real-world tablets to make it familiar and easy to use.
points: The virtual tablet interface is the main interface for navigation tools, a video player, and information content.
Navigation tools include a left-side island map and buttons to open the mini map.
The video player features a volume controller and other controls for viewing cultural or drone videos.
Information content is accessed through info elements.
The design is inspired by real-world tablets to make it familiar and easy to use.

data.text: Minimaps provide local orientation for specific places, allowing users to navigate through 360-degree images by following dots and using arrows. Notifications alert users to cultural videos available at specific spots. Global and local maps reduce clutter and provide wayfinding support by offering spatial orientation awareness.
points: Minimaps provide local orientation for specific places like villages or towns.
Users navigate through 360-degree images by following dots and using arrows for direction.
Notifications alert users to cultural videos available at specific spots.
Global and local maps reduce clutter and provide wayfinding support by offering spatial orientation awareness.

data.text: Moving between locations in the tour involves transitioning between 360-degree images using view interpolation to ensure smooth visual transitions. Navigation arrows guide the user between images to prevent random movement. To avoid the time and cybersickness of walking, a virtual vehicle metaphor is used for long-distance travel. This technique provides a seated viewpoint and allows for selection-based movement along pre-planned routes.
points: Moving between locations in the tour involves transitioning between 360-degree images.
View interpolation blurs boundaries to ensure smooth transitions and prevent jerks.
Navigation arrows guide the user between images to prevent random movement.
A virtual vehicle metaphor facilitates long-distance travel to avoid the time and cybersickness associated with walking.
The virtual vehicle technique provides a seated viewpoint and uses ray casting for selection-based movement on pre-planned routes.

data.text: The tablet interface provides location-relevant videos tailored by the user's location and type. Textual descriptions and notifications provide additional context about locations and significant spots. Directional arrows and information icons support point-of-interest awareness by guiding users toward locations and providing further details, mostly as textual information, so users do not overlook important elements.
points: The tablet interface provides location-relevant videos tailored by the user's location and type.
Textual descriptions and notifications provide additional context about locations and significant spots.

Directional arrows and information icons support point-of-interest awareness by guiding users toward locations and providing further details, mostly as textual information, so users do not overlook important elements.

data.text: Controlled navigation via joystick use or teleportation minimizes cybersickness by avoiding abrupt movements. Additionally, the speed of change of viewpoint in vehicular movement must be chosen carefully to avoid causing discomfort. Consistent visual cues and smooth transitions help maintain spatial orientation and reduce sensory conflicts.
points: Controlled navigation using a joystick or teleportation minimizes cybersickness by avoiding abrupt movements.
Vehicle movement speeds must be chosen carefully to avoid causing cybersickness.
Consistent visual cues and smooth transitions maintain spatial orientation and reduce sensory conflicts.

data.text: In the design of immersive experiences, the term design refers to interface and interaction design rather than code design.
points: Design in immersive experiences refers to interface and interaction design.
